# Copilot instructions

Security Resource Kit is a React/TypeScript learning site with a Hono Cloudflare Worker API and D1 storage. Reference text uses Verdana at 12 px with compact bold headings (125%/110%). Navigation/window controls use Tahoma; code uses Courier New. Preserve the square/beveled controls and left Contents/Index/Search navigation. Do not add decorative serif fonts, hero banners, marketing slogans, metaphors, or promotional headings. Use plain technical-reference language.

## Commands

Use Node >=22.12 and `npm ci`.

| Task | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Lint | `npm run lint` |
| Type-check all runtime contexts | `npm run typecheck` |
| Production build | `npm run build` |
| Unit suite | `npm test` |
| One unit case | `npm test -- security.test.ts -t "hashes tokens"` |
| Browser/API suite | `npm run test:e2e` |
| One browser scenario | `npm run test:e2e -- --grep "verified passkeys"` |
| Source drift | `npm run sources:check` |
| Approve a reviewed source | `npm run sources:approve -- identities` |
| Cloud provisioning / publication | `npm run cloud:setup`, then `npm run deploy` |

Browser tests use a dedicated `.wrangler\e2e-state` D1 database and virtual WebAuthn authenticators. Install Chromium only if the selected test reports a missing executable. Browser and Worker globals are separated in `tsconfig.app.json` and `tsconfig.worker.json`; combining them creates DOM/HTMLRewriter type collisions. Shared JSON imports use `with { type: 'json' }` so Node/Playwright and the bundlers can all consume them.

## Architecture

`shared\catalog.ts` is the server-only curriculum model. Never import it or the source registry into browser code. The client loads the catalog through authenticated `/api/catalog`; only sanitized top-level ID/title/status comes from public `/api/outline`. `content-types.ts` and `learning-utils.ts` contain data-free browser-safe contracts/helpers. `lesson.trackId` drives member navigation and discussion identities. Wire records and mutation acknowledgements are validated by `api-schemas.ts`.

Workers Assets serves public `dist` files; `/api/*` and member HTML routes run the Hono application. `access-policy.ts` defines the explicit public API/page allowlists and member routing patterns. Anonymous deep links redirect to the landing page; unknown APIs deny access by default. Auth, learning, discussions, account lifecycle, and source maintenance are separate modules over prepared D1 statements. Progress is member-only.

## Repository-specific invariants

- A gist and each prose nugget are <=100 words, enforced in unit and browser tests. All lessons use `shared\lesson-flow.ts`: one pre-topic question per page, summary, separate checkpoints/evidence/examples/exercise, one application question per page, then individual question/exercise reviews and topic completion. Never show correctness, feedback, scores, or exercise solutions before the final review. Incorrect diagnostic answers do not block signed-in reading. Preparation/application must save successfully before moving to content/review; unanswered Next stays disabled. Next topic starts its own preparation. Module completion uses current-revision server records, never client flags. Per-tab history may retain validated unsubmitted answer selections, scoped to account/lesson/revision, but cannot authorize reading or grant completion. Lesson discussions open separately, not beneath each nugget.
- Preserve stable track/lesson IDs when reorganizing navigation. Increment lesson revisions for material changes and set review dates only after technical review. Planned tracks must have no published lessons.
- Source definitions/fingerprints live in `shared\source-registry.json` and `shared\source-baselines.json`. Both fetchers use `shared\source-allowlist.json` for exact Microsoft hosts/path prefixes. Learn upstreams request `accept=text/markdown`; Graph references pin their API version. Daily checks flag changes or unavailability, never rewrite lessons or renew review dates. Extend the allowlist explicitly for a new primary source. Workers fetch does not support `redirect: 'error'`; use `manual` and reject redirect status codes.
- Split additional courses into `shared\courses` and import them only from the server catalog. Optional HTTP/KQL/JSON examples remain escaped plain text, use synthetic data or explicit templates, and cite a registered source. Set `documentationConflict: true` on evidence for discrepancies that must appear on the member-only References page.
- Registration supports configured Microsoft/GitHub accounts and optional passkeys, with current explicit policy acceptance and production Turnstile. Provider identity uses immutable issuer/subject hashes, never email/handle merges or provider role claims. No password/reset bypass, first-user admin, or employment verification exists. Linking/removal, exports/deletion, and moderation require recent site authentication.
- User/role authorization comes from the live D1 session join, not client fields. Every mutation requires the origin/JSON header boundary; authenticated mutations also require CSRF. Authenticated comments/questions/replies never use Turnstile; registration and public or signed-in private contact still verify real production Turnstile. Contributions are plain text, secret/control-checked, rate-limited, and pending until moderation, except a freshly authenticated pinned owner's initial announcement.
- Central `/discussions` and `/discussions/*` HTML routes must stay Worker-first in `access-policy.ts`, both `wrangler.toml` asset sections, and the cloud-setup generator. Forums derive from published catalog tracks plus Site discussions and Announcements. Course/lesson pages share one stable `page-<pageId>` conversation with the forum; other published pages map to Site discussions. Independent questions have a title and initial post. Never duplicate page comments into a category or import the server catalog into browser forum code.
- Reply topology is immutable, with root depth 0 and maximum server depth 16. Reject deeper replies explicitly; never truncate/reparent. Roots/threads paginate 30 newest-first, direct children 30 oldest-first. Cap visual indentation at six desktop/two mobile levels while displaying actual depth and parent links. Every ancestor must be visible before returning, reporting, or replying to a descendant. A moderator's member view has no private-branch override; its separate fresh-authorized queue includes thread/parent context.
- Migration 0004 is additive: preserve all existing comment IDs, bodies, statuses, reports, and review history. Legacy direct comment inserts attach as page roots. Anonymous `discussion_nodes` retain other members' parent relationships after account/content deletion, but no deleted personal text, title, handle, or author ID. Only a parent published at removal can leave a visible placeholder; deleted pending/hidden branches stay inaccessible and removed leaves are omitted. Prune only empty removed branches in affected threads, transactionally retaining all ancestors of remaining live posts, including private ones. Export the member's thread/category/parent/depth/title relationships. Repeat live session/consent and applicable pinned-owner/reviewer predicates inside transactional writes.
- Site management belongs only to verified personal GitHub ID `8750972` (`oguzhanf`), not `oguzhanf_microsoft`, a public handle/email, or a generic moderator role. Keep this pin server-only. The server returns the top-bar management link only for the owner; every management HTML/API request independently repeats the live identity check. Private management reads/actions require authentication within five minutes. GitHub is first, but passkey enrollment/sign-in must remain supported for all accounts.
- Guests see only a reduced, non-clickable topic tree, a brief free-registration landing page, terms/privacy policies, and the private contact form. Topics, references, discussions, and their APIs require a valid session. Do not reintroduce guest practice, public curriculum imports, or UI-only access checks. Clear member content after logout or session expiry.
- `/api/contact` is submission-only for visitors and always verifies production Turnstile/rate limits. Signed-in contact submissions require CSRF. Private request reads/resolution require fresh moderator authorization; never publish messages or reply addresses. Requests expire after 90 days.
- Visitor pages and public `/api/config` must not expose operator setup checklists, missing-secret details, or policy-approval instructions. Use brief availability messages for visitors; keep diagnostics in operator CLI/docs. Preserve the underlying launch gates.
- D1 `meta.changes` can include FK cascades. When asserting deletion of one parent record, use `DELETE ... RETURNING id` and inspect the returned identity, not `meta.changes === 1`.
- The toolchain overrides pin patched Undici 7.30.0, Sharp 0.35.5, and the official immutable source-map-js 1.2.2 security release. Preserve these until equally verified patched versions are available; never force an audit-driven Vite/Wrangler downgrade.
- Production session/passkey cookies use `__Host-`, Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite=Strict. The separate ten-minute OAuth flow cookie is Lax for the external GET callback and cannot authenticate member requests. Starts require the normal origin/JSON boundary; callbacks require provider/browser-bound one-use state, S256 PKCE, and verified identity. Microsoft verification must also enforce audience, tenant/issuer, signing-key issuer, expiry/issued time, and nonce. Provider exchanges reject redirects and oversized responses.
- Secrets belong in Worker secrets, never browser storage, Vite variables, source, command arguments, or production config JSON. Provider tokens are transient, never persisted or logged. Do not enable a provider until its dedicated app registration and exact callback are configured; do not replace a provider app ID without an identity migration. Preserve at least one currently available sign-in method during removals.
- Hosting is authenticated **permanent cloud deployment only**. Do not set up IIS, OS hosting services, tunnels, or an expiring `--temporary` account. Development/test runners are not deployment. Production participation fails closed until the operator reviews policies and supplies launch configuration.

`README.md` explains content authoring. `HOSTING.md` contains cloud launch/moderator/recovery commands. `SECURITY.md` documents the actual boundaries. Keep those and the rendered policy pages consistent with implementation changes.
